title: Differentiation and single-cell RNA-seq analyses of human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived renal organoids
protocol: Thaw Matrigel according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute thawed Matrigel to 0.02 mg/mL using cold (4°C) DMEM/F12.
Ensure that the Matrigel solution is well-mixed.
Store Matrigel solution on ice if it will not be used immediately.
Dispense half-well volume of Matrigel solution per well.
Incubate Matrigel-coated plates at room temperature for a minimum of 1 hour before use.
Remove vial of hPSCs from cryogenic storage.
Rapidly thaw hPSCs by swirling the vial gently in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer contents of vial to 15 mL conical tube containing 5 mL growth medium using a wide-bore P1000.
Use a wide-bore pipette tip when handling hPSC colonies.
Centrifuge hPSCs at 250 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Aspirate Matrigel solution from the culture vessel and replace with warmed growth medium to a volume equivalent to the well capacity.
Resuspend hPSCs in 1 mL of growth medium.
Dispense resuspended hPSCs into Matrigel-coated wells.
Transfer the plate to a hypoxic incubator set at 37°C, 5% O2, and 10% CO2.
Refresh the growth medium every 48 hours.
Inspect hPSC colonies for signs of differentiation before refreshing the medium.
Remove areas with differentiated cells by washing if spontaneous differentiation is moderate or higher.
Limit excessive cleaning of hPSC colonies to avoid cell death.
Refer to step 3 for specific instructions on removing spontaneously differentiated cells.
Add cell dissociation buffer (EDTA) to hPSC colonies with moderate differentiation.
Spray regions of differentiated cells repeatedly using a pipette.
Replace cell dissociation buffer with PBS and perform additional washing until most differentiated cells are removed.
Rinse remaining colonies gently with fresh PBS to remove non-adherent cells.
Return the plate to an incubator after adding growth medium.
Observe lifted edges of hPSC colonies reattaching to the plate.
Remove overgrown areas from hPSC colony by spraying repeatedly with a pipette tip.
Replace cell dissociation buffer with PBS and continue washing until overgrown areas are removed.
Inspect hPSCs under a microscope.
Identify overgrown regions in the colonies.
Wash colonies using dissociation buffer to remove overgrown areas.
Remove loosely adherent cells by running dissociation buffer down the side of each well.
Aspirate growth medium from the wells.
Replace with half-well volume of cell dissociation buffer.
Immediately use a pipette to spray areas containing overgrown and differentiated hPSC colonies with cell dissociation buffer 2 to 3 times.
Direct the spray at overgrown regions of hPSC colonies to wash away cells.
Spray gently initially, increasing force if necessary for detachment without washing away entire colony.
Inspect hPSCs under microscope.
If sufficient cleaning is achieved, proceed to next step; otherwise, repeat spraying or incubate at room temperature for 30 seconds and inspect again.
Avoid excessive detachment of undifferentiated hPSCs with cell dissociation buffer.
Do not proceed to passaging if hPSCs were incubated with cell dissociation buffer for longer than 3 minutes.
Aspirate cell dissociation buffer.
Rinse gently with PBS to remove loose cells.
Replace with 1x well volume of growth medium.
Return cells to hypoxic incubator.
Passage hPSC colonies.
Prepare Matrigel-coated plates as described in step 1 before proceeding.
Replace growth medium with half-well volume of cell dissociation buffer.
Perform wash steps as described in step 3 if necessary.
Incubate hPSCs with cell dissociation buffer for a maximum of 3 min.
Replace cell dissociation buffer with half-well volume of growth medium.
Use cell scraper to gently lift hPSC colonies.
Transfer hPSC colonies to a 15 mL conical tube containing 2 mL growth medium.
Scrape hPSCs gently and transfer using wide-bore P1000.
Pellet large hPSC aggregates by centrifugation at 250 g for 10–20 seconds.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend hPSCs in 1 mL growth medium.
Seed hPSC colonies into plates at a split ratio of 1:10 to 1:20.
Passage hPSCs at a split ratio to achieve 70–80% confluence in 3–4 days.
Transfer plate to normoxic incubator, 5% CO2, 21% O2.
Inspect cells for differentiation and wash as required.
Refresh growth medium every 48 hours.
Prepare growth, ROCKi & ABG media.
Replace the growth medium in each well containing hPSCs to be differentiated with half-well volume of ROCKi medium.
Return the wells to the normoxic incubator.
Incubate hPSCs with ROCKi medium for a minimum of 2 hours.
Dilute Matrigel to 0.5 mg/mL using cold DMEM/F12.
Dispense half-well volume of diluted Matrigel per well.
Keep Matrigel solution cold while working.
Ensure Matrigel solution is well-mixed.
Seal Matrigel-coated plates with parafilm and store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Incubate Matrigel-coated vessels at room temperature for a minimum of 1 hour before use.
Gently wash away overgrown areas of hPSC colonies, if necessary, by spraying with ROCKi medium in each well.
Aspirate wells and gently rinse with PBS to remove loose cells.
Add half-well volume of Accutase to each well and return cells to normoxic incubator for 10 minutes.
Tap side of plate and inspect cells.
Return cells to incubator for an additional 5 minutes if colonies are not completely dissociated into single cells.
Transfer dissociated hPSCs to a 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse wells with ROCKi medium and add to the tube.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 250 g for 5 minutes.
Count and seed cells.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL ROCKi medium using a wide-bore P1000.
Count cells and adjust volume to 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Aspirate Matrigel solution from organoid vessel.
Replace with 1x well volume of ROCKi medium.
Seed cells at desired density.
Rock plate gently to disperse cells.
Return plate to normoxic incubator overnight (12–24 h).
Overlay cells with Matrigel.
Dilute Matrigel to 0.25 mg/mL with cold growth medium.
Aspirate medium from organoid plate.
Replace with 1x well volume of cold Matrigel solution.
Return plates to incubator until day 4.
Prepare initiation medium as per the detailed recipe provided in the key resources table.
Treat cells with the prepared initiation medium.
Prepare initiation medium containing CHIR-99021 at an optimized concentration for the cell line of interest.
Aspirate Matrigel solution from organoid plate.
Replace with 2x well volume of initiation medium.
Return cells to incubator for 36–42 hours.
Aspirate initiation medium after 36–42 hours.
Replace with 2x well volume of ABG medium.
Return plates to incubator.
Aspirate all ABG medium from the wells after 48 hours.
Refresh with 1x well volume of ABG medium.
Refresh with 1x well volume of ABG medium every 48–72 hours.
Ensure solutions used are cooled and kept on ice before proceeding.
Pre-cool the centrifuge before use.
Prepare 25 μL of unique 10x barcoding solution per sample.
Prepare 25 μL of 10x co-anchor solution per sample.
Mix anchor LMO and barcode stock solutions at a 1:1 M ratio in PBS to achieve a final concentration of 2 μM for each sample.
Dilute the co-anchor LMO stock solution in PBS to achieve a final concentration of 2 μM for all samples.
Prepare 1% BSA in PBS.
Dissociate kidney organoids from each time point.
Aspirate ABG medium from well containing kidney organoids.
Rinse organoids gently with 1x well volume of PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add 1x well volume of Accutase.
Return organoids to incubator at 37°C for 15 min.
Use a 25g needle and syringe to triturate kidney organoids 3 times.
Triturate with a cell scraper if needed for large vessel sizes.
Transfer each dissociated sample into an individual labeled tube containing 5x well volume of cold PBS.
Keep samples on ice to minimize expression changes from processing.
Pellet samples by centrifugation at 250 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in approximately 125 μL of cold PBS.
Determine cell viability of each sample.
Aliquot 10 μL of cell suspension into a microcentrifuge tube.
Combine with 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue solution.
Count cells and determine sample viability.
Adjust concentration of sample cell suspension to 2.8 × 10^6 cells/mL using cold PBS.
Label each sample with a unique barcode.
Transfer 0.5 × 10^6 live cells to a labeled microfuge tube.
Adjust sample volume to 180 μL with cold PBS.
Add 20 μL of 10x Barcoding solution and mix gently.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Prepare a unique barcoding solution for each sample and record barcode-sample pairs.
Add 22.2 μL of 10x Co-Anchor solution and mix gently.
Incubate on ice for 5–10 minutes.
Add 900 μL of cold 1% BSA solution to each sample.
Centrifuge at 250 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove 1050 μL of supernatant, leaving 50 μL liquid and cell pellet in each tube.
Repeat the previous steps to remove unbound barcodes, leaving 80 μL liquid and cell pellet in each tube.
Triturate remaining solution with a wide bore p200 to resuspend cells.
Determine cell count and viability.
Combine 2 × 10^4 cells from each barcoded cell suspension in a single tube.
Adjust cell concentration of combined samples with cold 1% BSA solution to 1000 cells/μL.
Filter pooled and barcoded cell suspension through a 35 μm mesh cell strainer twice.
Submit pooled and barcoded cell suspension for library preparation and RNA sequencing.
Convert Illumina BCL files to FASTQ files using the mkfastq function in CellRanger software.
Generate raw count matrices with the count function.
Demultiplex samples using the standard MULTI-seq workflow.
Import data into R, using the Seurat 4.0 package and protocol published by Hao et al.
Plot smoothed density frequencies of cell quality control metrics including UMI counts.
Plot histograms of the number of uniquely detected genes for each cell.
Plot fractions of mitochondrial reads per cell.
Visually inspect the distributions to determine appropriate cut-off thresholds.
Remove cells falling outside designated thresholds from subsequent analyses.
Remove cells labeled “doublets” or “negatives” by the MULTI-seq analysis pipeline.
Normalize expression using the SCTransform function in Seurat.
Include a regression variable for the difference in cell cycle score between proliferating and non-proliferating cells.
Perform Principal Components Analysis (PCA).
Run the RunPCA function in Seurat.
Generate a Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) on 40 most variable PCA dimensions.
Run the RunUMAP function in Seurat.
Determine uniquely and highly expressed genes in each cluster.
Run the FindAllMarkers function in Seurat.
Visualize the top marker genes in each cluster based on prior biological knowledge.
Annotate top marker genes by comparing them to markers from other reported studies.
Infer cell differentiation trajectory using the learn_graph function in monocle3.
Assign a pseudotime value to each cell by using the order_cells function in monocle3 and select the root node (generally the earliest differentiation timepoint).
Perform trajectory analysis with the tradeSeq package.
Extract the expression and pseudotime values for each cell.
Determine the optimal number of knots empirically using the evaluateK function.
Select the smallest number of knots that reasonably minimizes the average Akaike Information Criterion (AIC).
Fit a Generalized Additive Model using the fitGAM function with the number of knots determined.
Use the associationTest function to find genes that vary significantly along the expression trajectory.
Transfect the CRISPR-CAS9 complex and ssDNA repair template into hPSCs.
Culture the transfected hPSCs to form colonies.
Select and screen the colonies for gene editing.
Introduce a double-stranded DNA break in the first exon shared across all TSC1 splice variants using CRISPR-CAS9.
Use an ssDNA repair template containing stop codons in all reading frames and a PmeI cut site for homology-directed repair of the DNA break.
Knock out the target gene and insert a PmeI cut site for subsequent screening in successfully edited cells.
Culture hPSCs as described in steps 1 to 4.
Passage hPSCs to achieve approximately 80% confluence before proceeding.
Seed hPSC cells for transfection into Matrigel-coated plates the day before transfection.
Incubate hPSCs with ROCKi medium for a minimum of 2 hours before dissociation.
Dissociate hPSC colonies into single cells and pellet as described in step 11.
Resuspend and count dissociated hPSC cells as described in step 12.
Seed cell suspension into Matrigel-coated plates containing 1x well volume ROCKi medium at concentrations of 2 × 10^4, 1 × 10^4, 0.5 × 10^4, and 0.025 × 10^4 cells/cm².
Aspirate ROCKi medium from plates and replace with 1x well volume growth medium.
Prepare transfection medium for tube 1: Mix 100 μL Opti-MEM I medium with 4 μL Lipofectamine Stem Reagent.
Prepare transfection medium for tube 2: Mix 100 μL Opti-MEM I medium with 2 μg CRISPR plasmid and 0.5 μL of ssODN (100 μM).
Transfer contents of tube 2 into tube 1 and mix by gently pipetting.
Incubate transfection medium for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 200 μl of transfection medium dropwise to each plate of cells.
Distribute drops of transfection medium evenly over entire plate, rock plate gently to ensure even distribution of the transfection complex across the entire plate.
Return cells to incubator overnight.
Aspirate transfection mix and replace with 1x well volume of fresh growth medium.
Refresh growth medium daily until ready for colony picking.
Aspirate media from transfected hPSCs.
Replace with 2x well volume ROCKi medium.
Return plate to hypoxic incubator for 1 hour.
Aspirate Matrigel solution from 96-well plate and replace with 1x well volume ROCKi medium.
Gently scrape off unique colonies using a p200 pipette and transfer each colony into a well of the 96-well plate.
Use a fresh pipette tip for each colony to avoid cross contamination.
Minimize the volume of ROCKi medium transferred along with the selected colony.
Refresh ROCKi medium if excessive numbers of floating cells are present.
Return 96-well plate containing picked colonies to hypoxic incubator overnight.
Aspirate ROCKi medium and replace with 1x well volume of growth medium.
Avoid cross contamination of cells between wells.
Refresh growth medium daily until wells reach approximately 80% confluence.
Prepare Matrigel-coated 96-well plates before proceeding.
Aspirate growth medium from the plate and replace with 30 μL Accutase.
Return colonies to incubator for 5 min.
Optionally, incubate colonies with ROCKi medium for 2 h before addition of Accutase if concerned about viability.
Aspirate Matrigel solution from 96-well plate and replace with 1x well volume ROCKi medium.
Gently aspirate off cell dissociation buffer after removing colonies from the incubator.
Slowly add 120 μL ROCKi medium to each well, avoiding aspiration of hPSC colonies.
Scrape and lift hPSC colonies using a p200 and gently tritrate by pipetting.
Transfer 40 μL into the new Matrigel-coated plate and 40 μL into the PCR plate.
Triturate colonies until they have lifted from the plate but remain as small aggregates, avoiding vigorous trituration to prevent breaking apart easily.
Return passaged hPSC colonies to hypoxic incubator and immediately proceed with extraction of genomic DNA from PCR plate.
Replace ROCKi medium with growth medium the next day.
Refresh growth medium daily.
Pellet cell suspension by centrifugation at 600 g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Add 5 μL of QuickExtract DNA solution to each well.
Seal the plate with film.
Vortex the plate to mix (15 seconds).
Pool liquid by centrifuging at 500 g for 15 seconds.
Incubate at 65°C for 6 minutes using a thermal cycler.
Vortex the plate again.
Pool liquid by centrifugation.
Incubate at 98°C for 2 minutes.
Vortex the plate once more.
Pool liquid by centrifugation.
Add 5 μL of PCR-grade H2O to each well.
Vortex the plate and pool liquid by centrifugation.
Prepare a OneTaq PCR master mix solution using primers specific to your mutation site.
Keep the PCR master mix on ice.
Perform PCR to screen for clones.
Add 18 μL of PCR master mix to each well of a 96-well PCR plate.
Transfer 2 μL of template DNA into each well.
Cover the plate with a PCR-compatible seal.
Vortex briefly and then centrifuge to pool liquid, 100 g for 30 seconds.
Place the plate in a thermocycler and perform PCR according to specified conditions.
Pause point: Store the PCR product at −20°C until ready to proceed.
Prepare a Digestion master mix solution as per Table 4 specifications.
Digest PCR reaction product by adding 10 μL of digestion master mix to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Transfer 5 μL from each well of the PCR-amplified reaction product into the digestion plate.
Seal the plate with film.
Vortex briefly and then centrifuge to pool liquid, 100 g for 30 seconds.
Incubate the plate in a thermocycler at 37°C for 1 hour.
Prepare 2% agarose gel using TBE buffer.
Pour the agarose gel with 4 × 26 slot combs, creating a total of 104 wells.
Add 3 μL of 6x loading dye to each well containing digested PCR product.
Load 10 μL of each sample into a well of the agarose gel.
For each row, add a DNA ladder in the first and last wells.
Perform gel electrophoresis at approximately 100 V for 1–2 hours, adjusting voltage if buffer heats up.
Visualize the gel using a UV transilluminator.
Dissociate wells containing mutants and seed at low density for colony formation.
Repeat colony picking and screening steps.
Perform subcloning to ensure monoclonal population isolation.
Validate isolated monoclonal population by Sanger sequencing and Western blot.
Submit sample for karyotyping.
Fix kidney organoids.
Add 1x well volume 8% (v/v) formaldehyde solution to differentiation vessel.
Incubate at room temperature for 45 min.
Aspirate fixation solution and replace with 2x well volume PBS.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Repeat washing by replacing the liquid in the wells with 2x well volume PBS, incubating at room temperature for 15 min, repeating this process a total of 5 times to remove excess formaldehyde.
Aspirate liquid from wells and replace with permeabilization + block solution (1% BSA, 0.1% TWEEN-20 in PBS).
Incubate at room temperature for 3 h.
Aspirate permeabilization solution and replace with block + wash solution (1% BSA, 0.01% TWEEN-20 in PBS).
Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Repeat the previous incubation step a total of 3 times.
Stain organoids with primary antibodies.
Dilute NPHS1 (podocyte marker) antibody in block + wash solution at a concentration of 1:100.
Dilute LRP2 (proximal tubule marker) antibody in block + wash solution at a concentration of 1:100.
Dilute CDH1 (distal tubule marker) antibody in block + wash solution at a concentration of 1:200.
Prepare a half-well volume of primary antibody solution for each well to be stained.
Aspirate the block + wash solution and replace with a half-well volume of primary antibody solution.
Incubate at 4°C overnight.
Wash organoids to remove excess antibody.
Aspirate the block + wash solution and replace with two times the well volume of fresh block + wash solution.
Repeat washing three more times by aspirating and replacing the solution each time.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 hours.
Repeat the previous incubation step a total of four times over an eight-hour period.
Stain organoids with appropriate fluorescently-tagged secondary antibodies.
Dilute secondary antibodies in block + wash solution at a concentration of 1:400.
Aspirate the block + wash solution and replace with a half-well volume of secondary antibody solution.
Incubate at 4°C overnight to remove excess antibody.
Repeat washing steps (step 79) to remove excess antibody completely.
Note: Optionally, add Hoechst 33343 at a concentration of 1:1000 to the block + wash solution.
If using Hoechst, perform one or two additional washes as needed.
Proceed directly to imaging if kidney organoids were stained in optical-bottom plates.
Mount kidney organoids under coverslips prior to imaging if not already done.
Image kidney organoids using fluorescence or confocal microscopy.
